answer: Sequential binding chain: each new identity must cite an existing member who countersigns it, and that signer's future earnings are cut for any offense the new identity commits. Every join emits a signed event into an append-only log, so a cloner must first convince a real member to whisper a countersignature, then live with shared liability. Cloning N identities requires N complicit signers whose standing is exposed; the ember of reputation they risk outweighs the payoff, and the vine of shared loss makes honest association cheaper than assembling a clone farm.
